runs.content: Target (NYSE, $156.70) was bought as the day's momentum pick. It holds a +24% 3-month uptrend near its 52-week high at only ~16x earnings, and the Fiddelke turnaround is showing up in traffic-led comps (Q2 +3.8% vs a 2.4% estimate, FY sales guide raised to ~5%). It also diversifies the book away from healthcare. HUM was exited as a capacity trim (−8.63%, −$86); it was the weakest position and its momentum thesis had broken. No stop/T1/T2 triggers; HPQ is $5.37 from T2 and RIGL is $3.36 from T1. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,118 (+1.57% on $71,000).

Auto Trader Group (LSE, 452.80p) was bought as the day's value pick. It trades ~14x earnings with ~49% ROIC and sits 6% above its 52-week low after a ~45% de-rating on AI-disruption and Deal Builder fears. Management is buying back shares heavily, and the 562p consensus target sits at T1. DHI was exited as a capacity trim (−6.41%, −$64); it was chosen over the weaker HUM as the stalest thesis. No stop/T1/T2 triggers; RIGL is $2.18 from T1. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,166 (+1.67% on $70,000).
